cdf_model <- subset(c_cardiodf, select = -c(id, dataset, num, ca)) #decided to remove ca, also removing num cause now we have binary target

glimpse(cdf_model)
## Rows: 920
## Columns: 13
## $ age      <int> 63, 67, 67, 37, 41, 56, 62, 57, 63, 53, 57, 56, 56, 44, 52, 5…

str(cdf_model)
## 'data.frame':    920 obs. of  13 variables:
##  $ age     : int  63 67 67 37 41 56 62 57 63 53 ...
##  $ sex     : chr  "Male" "Male" "Male" "Male" ...
##  $ cp      : chr  "typical angina" "asymptomatic" "asymptomatic" "non-anginal" ...
##  $ trestbps: int  145 160 120 130 130 120 140 120 130 140 ...
##  $ chol    : int  233 286 229 250 204 236 268 354 254 203 ...
##  $ fbs     : logi  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE ...
##  $ restecg : chr  "lv hypertrophy" "lv hypertrophy" "lv hypertrophy" "normal" ...
##  $ thalch  : int  150 108 129 187 172 178 160 163 147 155 ...
##  $ exang   : logi  FALSE TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE ...
##  $ oldpeak : num  2.3 1.5 2.6 3.5 1.4 0.8 3.6 0.6 1.4 3.1 ...
##  $ slope   : chr  "downsloping" "flat" "flat" "downsloping" ...
##  $ thal    : chr  "fixed defect" "normal" "reversable defect" "normal" ...
##  $ target  : num  0 1 1 0 0 0 1 0 1 1 ...
# changing target to factor for modelling; will do for some categorical variables too
cdf_model$target <- as.factor(cdf_model$target)
#true/false variables to no/yes
cdf_model$fbs <- factor(cdf_model$fbs, 
                        levels = c(FALSE, TRUE), 
                        labels = c("No", "Yes"))

cdf_model$exang <- factor(cdf_model$exang, 
                          levels = c(FALSE, TRUE), 
                          labels = c("No", "Yes"))
# categorical variables ; the rest of them; some have 

cdf_model$sex <- as.factor(cdf_model$sex)
cdf_model$cp <- as.factor(cdf_model$cp)
cdf_model$restecg <- as.factor(cdf_model$restecg)
cdf_model$slope <- as.factor(cdf_model$slope)
cdf_model$thal <- as.factor(cdf_model$thal)

str(cdf_model)
## 'data.frame':    920 obs. of  13 variables:
##  $ age     : int  63 67 67 37 41 56 62 57 63 53 ...
##  $ sex     : Factor w/ 2 levels "Female","Male": 2 2 2 2 1 2 1 1 2 2 ...
##  $ cp      : Factor w/ 4 levels "asymptomatic",..: 4 1 1 3 2 2 1 1 1 1 ...
##  $ trestbps: int  145 160 120 130 130 120 140 120 130 140 ...
##  $ chol    : int  233 286 229 250 204 236 268 354 254 203 ...
##  $ fbs     : Factor w/ 2 levels "No","Yes": 2 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 ...
##  $ restecg : Factor w/ 4 levels "","lv hypertrophy",..: 2 2 2 3 2 3 2 3 2 2 ...
##  $ thalch  : int  150 108 129 187 172 178 160 163 147 155 ...
##  $ exang   : Factor w/ 2 levels "No","Yes": 1 2 2 1 1 1 1 2 1 2 ...
##  $ oldpeak : num  2.3 1.5 2.6 3.5 1.4 0.8 3.6 0.6 1.4 3.1 ...
##  $ slope   : Factor w/ 4 levels "","downsloping",..: 2 3 3 2 4 4 2 4 3 2 ...
##  $ thal    : Factor w/ 4 levels "","fixed defect",..: 2 3 4 3 3 3 3 3 4 4 ...
##  $ target  : Factor w/ 2 levels "0","1": 1 2 2 1 1 1 2 1 2 2 ...
library(corrplot)
## Warning: package 'corrplot' was built under R version 4.3.3
## corrplot 0.92 loaded
cdf_cor <- cdf_model
cdf_cor[] <- lapply(cdf_cor, as.numeric)

cor_result <- cor(cdf_cor, use = "complete.obs")

# Simple corrplot - adding a title to make it look official
corrplot(cor_result, method = "circle", 
         tl.col = "black", title = "Variable Correlations", mar=c(0,0,1,0))

#cleaner 
corrplot(cor_result, method = "circle", 
         tl.col = "black", type = "upper", title = "Variable Correlations", mar=c(0,0,1,0))

set.seed(42) #the ultimste question to life..universe...everything

#split 80-20
split_index <- createDataPartition(cdf_model$target, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)
train <- cdf_model[split_index, ]
test <- cdf_model[-split_index, ]
#crosschecking if they add up to 920! becasue that's the df population
dim(train)
## [1] 737  13
dim(test)
## [1] 183  13
colSums(is.na(cdf_model))
##      age      sex       cp trestbps     chol      fbs  restecg   thalch 
##        0        0        0       59       30       90        0       55 
##    exang  oldpeak    slope     thal   target 
##       55       62        0        0        0
View(cdf_model)
#FINALLLYYY i will handle the missing data with median and mode imputation to prevent loss of statistical power and valuable data

#numeric (median imputation):

#for resting blood pressure values
trestbps_med <- median(train$trestbps, na.rm = TRUE)
train$trestbps[is.na(train$trestbps)] <- trestbps_med
test$trestbps[is.na(test$trestbps)] <- trestbps_med

#for serum cholesterol values
chol_med <- median(train$chol, na.rm = TRUE)
train$chol[is.na(train$chol)] <- chol_med
test$chol[is.na(test$chol)] <- chol_med

#for maximum heart rate achieved
thalch_med <- median(train$thalch, na.rm = TRUE)
train$thalch[is.na(train$thalch)] <- thalch_med
test$thalch[is.na(test$thalch)] <- thalch_med

#for ST depression via exercise
oldpeak_med <- median(train$oldpeak, na.rm = TRUE)
train$oldpeak[is.na(train$oldpeak)] <- oldpeak_med
test$oldpeak[is.na(test$oldpeak)] <- oldpeak_med


#categorical (mode imputation):

#for fasting blood sugar
fbs_mode <- names(sort(table(train$fbs), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
train$fbs[is.na(train$fbs)] <- fbs_mode
test$fbs[is.na(test$fbs)] <- fbs_mode

#for exercies induced angina
exang_mode <- names(sort(table(train$exang), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
train$exang[is.na(train$exang)] <- exang_mode
test$exang[is.na(test$exang)] <- exang_mode
#double checking- ALL 0
colSums(is.na(train))
##      age      sex       cp trestbps     chol      fbs  restecg   thalch 
##        0        0        0        0        0        0        0        0 
##    exang  oldpeak    slope     thal   target 
##        0        0        0        0        0
colSums(is.na(test))
##      age      sex       cp trestbps     chol      fbs  restecg   thalch 
##        0        0        0        0        0        0        0        0 
##    exang  oldpeak    slope     thal   target 
##        0        0        0        0        0
#time to begin modeling
num_vars <- c("age", "trestbps", "chol", "thalch", "oldpeak")
prep <- preProcess(train[, num_vars], method = c("center", "scale"))
  
#scale for svm and LogR
train_scale <- predict(prep, train)
test_scale  <- predict(prep, test)
#checking...
summary(train_scale$chol) #mean is 0; good
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
## -1.8502 -0.2017  0.2059  0.0000  0.6042  3.6723
#Logistic Regression

cardio_logm <- glm(target ~., data = train_scale, family = binomial)

summary(cardio_logm)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = target ~ ., family = binomial, data = train_scale)

## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 12
#predict/probability

cardiologm_probs <- predict(cardio_logm, test_scale, type = "response")
cardiologm_pred <- ifelse(cardiologm_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)
cardiologm_pred <- factor(cardiologm_pred, levels = c(0,1))

confusionMatrix(cardiologm_pred, test_scale$target, positive = "1")
## Confusion Matrix and Statistics
## 
##           Reference
## Prediction  0  1
##          0 69 13
##          1 13 88
##                                          
##                Accuracy : 0.8579         
##                  95% CI : (0.7988, 0.905)
##     No Information Rate : 0.5519         
##     P-Value [Acc > NIR] : <2e-16         
##                                          
##                   Kappa : 0.7128         
##

#XGBoost
x_train <- model.matrix(target ~ . - 1, data=train)
x_test  <- model.matrix(target ~ . - 1, data=test)

y_train <- as.numeric(as.character(train$target))
y_test  <- as.numeric(as.character(test$target))

#Dmatrix
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = x_train, label = y_train)
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(data = x_test, label = y_test)
all(colnames(x_train) == colnames (x_test))
## [1] TRUE
set.seed(42)
param <- list(objective = "binary:logistic",
                      eval_metric = "logloss", 
                      max_depth = 5,
                      eta = 0.05, 
                      subsample = 0.8, 
                      colsample_bytree = 0.8, seed = 42)

wl <- list(train = dtrain, test=dtest)

cardio_xgb <- xgb.train(params = param,
                      data = dtrain, 
                      nrounds = 600, evals = wl,
                      early_stopping_rounds = 40,
                      verbose = 0)
cardioxgb_prob <- predict(cardio_xgb, x_test)
cardioxgb_pred <- factor(ifelse(cardioxgb_prob > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))


confusionMatrix(cardioxgb_pred, factor(y_test, levels = c(0, 1)), positive = "1")

#SHAP (XGBoost)- system analysis feature importance for explainability
pred_fun <- function(object, newdata) {
  predict(object, xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(newdata)))
}

set.seed(42)
sample_idx <- sample(1:nrow(x_train), min(300, nrow(x_train)))

X_shap <- as.data.frame(x_train[sample_idx, ])

shap_vals <- fastshap::explain(
  object = cardio_xgb,
  feature_names = colnames(x_train),
  X = X_shap,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  nsim = 50
)

imp <- sort(colMeans(abs(shap_vals)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
imp
##     cpatypical angina                  chol              exangYes 
##            0.07802927            0.06962961            0.06935396 
##               oldpeak                   age         cpnon-anginal 
##            0.04842642            0.04642087            0.03322939 
## thalreversable defect             sexFemale                thalch 
##            0.03182162            0.02986244            0.02727303 
##             slopeflat 
##            0.02688729
par(mar = c(10, 4, 4, 2))
barplot(imp, las = 2, col = "lightsalmon", cex.names = 0.8, main = "Top SHAP Feature Importance via XGBoost")
